typology.designNote: SVO with postpositional phrases was chosen (AI design decision, project spec §18) to keep the engine's grammar deterministic and learnable while remaining distinct from both English and Dutch surface order inside noun phrases.

pronouns.reflexive: suffix -ûm attached to the pronoun, e.g. 'zhâûm' = himself/herself/itself

nouns.pluralRule: Attach -ûk to the noun root; if the root already ends in -k, insert epenthetic -a- (-akûk) to avoid a geminate cluster.
nouns.definiteness: No articles. Definiteness is contextual, as in many isolating languages; a noun is read as definite unless context or an explicit demonstrative marks it otherwise.

possession.example: khar ta shak = "the king's strength" (literally "strength of king")
possession.pronominalAlternative: A possessive suffix (see pronouns.possessiveSuffixes) may attach directly to the possessum instead of using 'ta' when the possessor is a pronoun: 'kharaz' = "his/her/its strength".

nouns.compounding: Compound nouns are formed head-final: modifier + head, both roots joined directly, e.g. 'ghûl' (shadow) + 'dor' (land) = 'ghûldor' (shadowland).

verbs.imperative: bare root, sentence-initial, no subject pronoun required

aspect.habitual: reduplicate the first consonant+vowel of the root before the tense suffix, e.g. 'khaur' (burn) -> 'khakhaurak' (used to burn / burned repeatedly)

mood.conditional: particle 'ith' introduces the conditional clause; the result clause is unmarked, e.g. 'ith tû pâku, ük magâth' = "if you go, I will follow"

verbs.personNumberMarking: Verbs do not agree with person or number; the subject pronoun or noun phrase carries that information. This is a deliberate analytic design choice to keep the morphology regular and the translation engine fully deterministic.

irregulars.note: present tense is 'ash' itself (zero further suffix); past 'ashak'; future 'ashâth'.

superlative.marker: suffix -gûl added to the adjective in addition to 'zan'

adverbs.formation: derived from adjectives with the suffix -ith, e.g. 'khar' (strong) -> 'kharith' (strongly)
adverbs.position: typically follow the verb they modify

numerals.ordinalSuffix: -ith (same surface form as the adverbial suffix, disambiguated by syntactic position directly before a noun)
numerals.position: cardinal numerals precede the noun they quantify; ordinals also precede the noun

syntax.contentQuestion: Question word fronted to clause-initial position, remainder follows declarative order
syntax.conditional: 'ith' + protasis clause + comma-equivalent pause + apodosis clause
syntax.relativeClause: Formed with the relativiser 'kha' placed after the head noun: '[head noun] kha [clause]', e.g. 'shak kha khar dûnu' = "the king who has strength"
syntax.compoundSentenceExample: ük pâku ag tû magu = "I go and you follow"
syntax.complexSentenceExample: ük zûrak sû tû pâkâth = "I know that you will go"
